stick_manufacturing_sigma_control_limits.question: Manufacturing - sigma, control limits, capability, stack-up
references: W. A. Shewhart, Economic Control of Quality of Manufactured Product (1931)
M. J. Harry & R. Schroeder, Six Sigma (2000) - the 1.5-sigma shift convention
ISO 22514-2:2013 process capability; V. E. Kane, Process capability indices, J. Qual. Tech. 18 (1986) 41
ASME Y14.5 and the RSS method (Bender, SAE 1962)
stick_manufacturing_sigma_control_limits.statement: Quality is the normal distribution applied to a specification: defects per million map to sigma, limits sit at three sigma, capability is the spec width over six sigma, and independent tolerances add in quadrature.

ticks.claim: [six sigma, SEALED] 3.4 defects per million opportunities is the six-sigma level (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY). The number carries Motorola's 1.5-sigma shift: a process whose mean drifts 1.5 sigma still has 4.5 sigma to the nearer limit, and the normal tail beyond 4.5 sigma is 3.4 per million.
[five sigma, SEALED] 233 per million (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY).
[four sigma, SEALED] 6,210 per million (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY): one part in 161.

[three sigma, SEALED] 66,807 per million (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY) - about 6.7 percent defective, the level most unmanaged processes run at. Each sigma is an order of magnitude; the table is the normal distribution's tail read as a ladder.

[Shewhart's limits, SEALED] Mean 100, sigma 2: UCL = 106, LCL = 94 (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY). Three sigma either side leaves 0.27 percent of a stable process outside - a point beyond the line is a signal, not noise, and the operator looks for a cause (Shewhart 1931).
[capable, SEALED] Spec 90-110, process centred at 100 with sigma 2: Cp = 20 / 12 = 1.667 and Cpk = 1.667, capable against the 1.33 threshold (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY).

[not capable, SEALED AS NOT CAPABLE] The same spread centred at 106: Cp is still 1.667 but Cpk = (110 - 106) / 6 = 0.667 - NOT capable, sealed with claimed false (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY). Cp measures the spread, Cpk the spread AND the centring; a tight process in the wrong place still makes scrap.

[a tolerance stack, SEALED] Three parts toleranced 0.010, 0.020 and 0.015: the statistical stack is sqrt(0.0001 + 0.0004 + 0.000225) = 0.02693 (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY), against a worst case of 0.045.

[equal tolerances, SEALED] Three at 0.1: RSS = 0.1 sqrt 3 = 0.17321 (sealed through manufacturing.MFG_VERIFY) versus 0.3 worst case. Independent errors add in quadrature - the same sqrt N as random walks and measurement means.

[the conventions, CITED] The 1.5-sigma shift (Harry & Schroeder), three-sigma limits (Shewhart), the 1.33 capability threshold (Kane 1986, ISO 22514) and RSS stacking all ASSUME a normal, stable, independent process. They work, so a process that meets them is inferred capable, never proven so: a non-normal or drifting process breaks every number above. The engine seals the arithmetic the conventions command and declines the assumption.
ticks.source: Shewhart (1931); Harry & Schroeder, Six Sigma (2000); Kane, J. Qual. Tech. 18 (1986) 41; ISO 22514-2

ticks.claim: [on the one map] Every number here is the normal distribution's (card_floor_statistics: the tail integral, the sigma, quadrature addition) applied to a drawing's tolerance. The statistics stick holds the distribution; this stick holds the shop floor's use of it.
